newsitem.title: UK: LME copper, nickel extend decline late.
newsitem.headline: LME copper, nickel extend decline late.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) three-months copper tried the upside on Monday but lost momentum and sank in late trading.
Copper failed to breach tough support at $2,490 and eventually settled the kerb at $2,474 per tonne. It eased again in late inter-office activity and was bid at $2,466 by 1800 GMT when Comex closed.
"Volumes are quite light, with most of Europe on holiday, and the buying ran out in the afternoon," a trader said.
Brokerage Rudolf Wolff said, however, that the potential for price spikes was to be expected for some time, citing the continued draw on LME stocks and labour unrest in the Americas.
Nickel had dazzled early on with an advance to the highest in nearly two months after breaching resistance at $7,900.
But profit taking reversed the trend and nickel shed most of its gains by the close, ending the kerb just $35 firmer at $7,855.
Nickel also continued to slip in late inter-office activity and was bid at $7,820 by 1900 GMT. Aluminium was little changed from the kerb close at around $1,648.
